key_insight: Odd viscosity and odd elasticity support distinct wave-turbulence cascades that can be captured analytically by kinetic equations, yielding anisotropic direct energy transport in 3D and an inverse wave-action cascade in quasi-1D.
engineering_relevance: These results give a predictive framework for designing and diagnosing chiral active materials and metamaterials where non-reciprocal stresses control how fluctuations and energy move across scales.
method: Derive kinetic equations for weakly nonlinear random waves in odd-fluid and odd-solid models.
Solve the resulting Kolmogorov–Zakharov spectra analytically for three-wave and six-wave interaction regimes.
Compare the predicted cascade directions and spectra with direct numerical simulations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the analytical KZ spectra match direct numerical simulations for both odd viscosity (forward cascade) and odd elasticity (inverse cascade).
watch_item: The forward-cascade KZ solution for odd elasticity is nonlocal and therefore unphysical, while the valid inverse-cascade solution is only marginally nonlocal and requires a logarithmic correction.
paper_title: Wave turbulence theory of odd fluids and solids: kinetic equations and solutions
